newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds firm, futures nudging resistance.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds firm, futures nudging resistance.

text.p: Australian bonds attracted a modest bid tone at the opening in what is likely to be a more subdued session after this week's volatile trade.
Futures were attempting to extend Thursday's rally, nudging resistance at 92.360 on the June 10-year bond contract and 93.31 on the three-year position.
"The feeling is the market fell too far after the budget. We saw some stops taken out yesterday and the market is well support just below current levels," one trader said.
A recovery in U.S. Treasuries after a mixed batch of data was also lending support.

Bill futures retained their bid tone after Thursday's whippy action which coincided with a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane and lessening concerns that the Federal Reserve will tighten policy at next Tuesday's policy making meeting.
Although Macfarlane reiterated his concerns over wages growth, he also said that the central bank would let the economy run faster as long as they saw no damage to inflation.

The market will be closely watching next Thursday's final wages data for the February quarter to see if there is any revision to the strong 4.6 percent preliminary annual outcome and the breakdown between public and private wages.

Local debt continued Thursday's outperformance against the U.S., taking the 10-year spread to its lowest level since late April. The U.S. weakened on a jump in core April CPI and a drop in jobless claims, but rebounded flat industrial production, a fall in capacity utilisation and a recovery in the dollar.
